"I have no plan B except to continue my studies at the Academy," said Theodor. "If it were up to me, I would have left the Academy long ago, Agnes."

But Theodor could no longer afford to leave the Academy.

Training as a mage cost an incredible amount. Hundreds of etons. And so at the entrance examinations, thousands competed not only for a place at the Academy but for the Royal Grant: the Gold Academician's Card.

It covered not only tuition but the cost of living in Seraph, which was utterly unaffordable for a subseraph or a soul from Tverd. The Card's limit widened with every circle completed, allowing one to live in Seraph on an ever grander scale and to pay ever more expensive tuition fees. For Academy residents, the Card even covered expenses such as designer clothing and cozy homes.

And as long as one remained at the Academy, one need never even pay interest on a debt that grew endlessly. For nothing in Seraph was ever given freely.

The only problem was staying at the Academy, which was not so simple. Starting from the second circle, a mage was already fully qualified to work, but from the fourth, one could say goodbye to any hope of repaying one's debts. Demand for mages was high, but most of the work was not the study of the Plans' secrets, poetry, or metaphysical wandering through the thin layers of the True Plan. Those were pursuits that only accredited Academicians supported by Seraph could afford.

After all, someone had to repair the megabarges. Torture demons. Fight the Disorder, patching holes in the fabric of the world. Sort through the scavengers' hauls from the Shards in search of treasure, or at least LED bulbs. Carve ingredients for heart-healing elixirs out of corpses...

Agnes let the pause stretch long enough for effect, letting Theodor marinate in the unenviable prospects of one who had been expelled from the Academy even before the fifth circle.
